name: Rushil Goel
profile: Former Samsara executive who co-founded Nirvana Insurance in 2021 with Abhay Mitra and Alex Carges. Nirvana uses telematics data from trucks to price and manage commercial trucking insurance; it sold its first policy in 2022 and in December 2025 raised a $100M Series D led by Valor Equity Partners at a $1.5B valuation (Hurun lists ~$2B).
interesting_fact: Nirvana's Series D nearly doubled its valuation just over nine months after an $80M Series C at about $830M.
deep_cut_fact: The idea for Nirvana came while he was building Samsara's fleet business from scratch: he saw that trucking fleets and insurers were ignoring the telematics data from what is forecast to be 50 billion connected devices by 2030 when predicting risk.
notes: Profile sites say he studied CS at IIT Bombay, started a PhD at MIT, has a Wharton MBA, worked at BCG and Ola, and co-founded AirCare Labs. I could not confirm these against a primary source. Press route: press@nirvanatech.com.

name: Serge Lukyanov
current_role: Co-founder, Preply (current operating role not confirmed; not on Preply's leadership page)
profile: Ukrainian co-founder (also spelled Sergey Lukyanov/Lukianov) of Preply, the online language-tutoring marketplace he started in Kyiv in 2012 with Kirill Bigai and Dmytro Voloshyn, where he led product design. Preply hit a $1.2B valuation in January 2026 after a $150M Series D led by WestCap.
interesting_fact: Preply now connects learners with about 100,000 tutors and became one of the few Ukrainian-founded unicorns, keeping roughly 150 staff in Kyiv during the war.
notes: Lowest-profile of the three Preply founders; profile sites say he was previously a web designer at TemplateMonster and later Preply's head of product design, but I found no primary source. A LinkedIn profile (ua.linkedin.com/in/sergeylukyanov) appears in search results, but I could not confirm it is his. Best route is probably via Preply press or Kirill Bigai.

name: Joanna Strober
profile: Silicon Valley investor-turned-founder who previously built Kurbo Health, a digital childhood-obesity program sold to WW. She started Midi Health, a virtual clinic for women in perimenopause and menopause, after struggling to get good care for her own symptoms at 47. Midi operates in all 50 US states and raised a $100M Series D in February 2026 at a valuation above $1B.
interesting_fact: Midi grew out of her own frustration: at 47 she had insomnia and brain fog and could not find doctors who would properly treat her menopause symptoms.
deep_cut_fact: Long before Midi, she co-wrote the 2009 book 'Getting to 50/50: How Working Parents Can Have It All' with former Goldman Sachs MD Sharon Meers; a later edition has a foreword by Sheryl Sandberg. She also founded a 'working stiffs' moms' group.
notes: Very media-friendly; frequent podcast guest (Kara Goldin, Katie Couric, PBS, TechCrunch). Press route: media@joinmidi.com. A March 2026 release reportedly names JBC (midi@jbc-pr.com) as the PR agency, but I did not open that release to confirm it.
